clue.text: Sticks around, excessively pleased with oneself

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the word for sticks the other way round

parts.note: to gum things is to stick them together, so sticks means gums

explanation.surface: Someone clinging on while looking far too pleased with themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'around' turns GUMS (sticks) back to front.
explanation.definitionFit: A complacent, self-satisfied person is described as smug; the phrase is a straight synonym.

clue.text: Get rid of drug in a tight spot

parts.note: to scrap something is to get rid of it
E is slang for the drug ecstasy

explanation.surface: Disposing of narcotics while in a difficult situation.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrape is an awkward predicament, a synonym for a tight spot or fix.

clue.text: Aesthete and student seduced by slim French relative

indicators.note: a student seduced by something is drawn into it, so L goes inside the word for slim

parts.note: to slim is to diet
L is a learner, the crossword student
tante is French for aunt

explanation.surface: An art lover and a student led astray by a slender French aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'seduced by' puts L inside DIET to make DILET.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilettante is a dabbler in the arts, an amateur lover of beauty, much like an aesthete.

indicators.note: report signals that what is spoken is heard as another word

parts.note: a place is a position or rank in a contest

explanation.surface: An account of a fish with a foul smell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Report' signals that PLACE (rank) is said out loud and heard as the fish.
explanation.definitionFit: Plaice is a flatfish common in British waters, an example of a fish.

indicators.note: to work something is to shape and rework it, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Incomplete work being done on the American intelligence agency.
explanation.walkthrough: 'work' rearranges the letters of ON THE CIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Inchoate means just begun and not fully formed, so unfinished is a fair synonym.

indicators.note: purses means holds in, as lips are pursed, so the word trousered holds the answer within it

explanation.surface: A drug addict pocketing handbags in their trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A user is someone who takes drugs habitually, a common slang synonym for an addict.

clue.text: Two states about to desert Obama?

parts.note: DE is Delaware and MO is Missouri, two US state abbreviations
DE is Delaware and MO is Missouri, two US state abbreviations
C is circa, Latin for about
to rat is to desert one's side

explanation.surface: Asks whether a president is a man of two states about to abandon them.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark shows Obama is an example: he is a member of the US Democratic Party.
explanation.definitionFit: Barack Obama belongs to the Democratic Party, so he is an example of a party member.

parts.note: B is black, as on pencils
taken as written

explanation.surface: A bruised face, black and blue.
explanation.walkthrough: Blue was a British boy band; the question mark marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: Blue was a pop group of the early 2000s, so it is an example of a musical group.

clue.text: Prime Minister, once married to Camilla, changed name

indicators.note: changed tells us these letters are rearranged into a different order

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A former premier once wed to Camilla took a new name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'changed' rearranges CAMILLA into ACMILLA, between M and N. Harold Macmillan was UK Prime Minister 1957-63.
explanation.definitionFit: Harold Macmillan led the British government in the late 1950s, a former holder of the top office.

clue.text: Biblical kingdom with Hebrews in it

indicators.note: in here means the Hebrews abbreviation sits inside the letters for it

parts.note: it means sex appeal, abbreviated SA
Heb is the standard abbreviation for the book of Hebrews

explanation.surface: An ancient realm with Jewish people living there.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it' as sex appeal (SA) is a crossword staple.
explanation.definitionFit: Sheba is the Old Testament realm whose queen visited Solomon.

definitions.meaning: reserved here means serious and solemn in manner
a pit in which a body is interred

explanation.definitionFit: A grave manner is serious and restrained; a grave is also the hole where the dead are buried.

parts.note: a means one, the numeral I
Antony Sher was a celebrated British stage actor
Sir Henry Wood was the conductor who founded the Proms

explanation.surface: A list of three artists: an actor, a conductor and a writer.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as three people; in fact the first two build the third.
explanation.definitionFit: Christopher Isherwood wrote Goodbye to Berlin, so he is a writer of fiction.

definitions.note: read as Perhaps Olivier is: the Olivier is one stage of the National Theatre

indicators.note: performing suggests these letters putting on a turn in a new order

explanation.surface: Asks whether Laurence Olivier is on stage at three o'clock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'performing' rearranges AT THREE. Olivier looks like the actor, but the Olivier is an auditorium at London's National Theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Olivier is a playhouse auditorium named after the actor, an example of a venue for plays.

indicators.note: bound means surrounded, so the word for sharp encloses the letter for over

parts.note: sharp in taste is tart
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A cheating card player is bound over by the court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Card sharp' looks like one person; split it. 'bound' wraps TART round O.
explanation.definitionFit: A tarot is one of the picture cards used in fortune-telling, so it is a card.

clue.text: A trashy novel not often seen in public now

definitions.text: not often seen in public now

indicators.note: novel means new, so these letters take a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A trashy novel is rarely read in public these days.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' rearranges A TRASHY. Smoking bans have pushed the item out of pubs.
explanation.definitionFit: Since public smoking bans, the dish for cigarette ends is rarely found in public places.

parts.note: a house is a family line, as in the House of Windsor
mates are friends

explanation.surface: A list of the people we live among: relatives, pals and flatmates.
explanation.definitionFit: People who share a home are cohabitants; the word is a direct synonym.

clue.text: Vote in favour of holding a king for a long time

indicators.note: holding means the votes contain the king inside them

parts.note: yeas are votes in favour
R is rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: Supporting a monarch over a long reign.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' links; 'years' as in 'it took years' means a long time.
explanation.definitionFit: Saying something took years means it took a long time, an idiomatic sense.

indicators.note: on the contrary tells us to swap a word for its opposite, here the off for on

parts.note: a rip-off is a swindle

explanation.surface: Asks if the city is a con, then denies it.
explanation.walkthrough: RIPON is a cathedral city in North Yorkshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Ripon is a small cathedral city in Yorkshire, an example of a city.

parts.note: proteas are South African flowering shrubs

indicators.note: start to means the first letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Plants begin to secrete a digestive chemical.
explanation.definitionFit: A protease is an enzyme that breaks down proteins, so it is a kind of enzyme.

indicators.note: third here means the first third of the word, three of its nine letters

explanation.surface: A man humming Beethoven's Third Symphony.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Third' looks like the Eroica symphony; it is the first third of BEETHOVEN.
explanation.definitionFit: A bee is the insect that buzzes as it flies, so it hums.

clue.text: Reproductive activity described by euphemism — or in a coarse way?

indicators.note: described by means drawn round, so the euphemism encloses the activity

parts.note: bally is an old British euphemism for bloody
the rut is the breeding season of deer

explanation.surface: Asks whether talking of sex by euphemism is crude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'described by' uses describe's geometric sense, to draw round, not to portray; the question mark admits the definition is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: Acting brutally means acting savagely and roughly, a fair sense of coarse behaviour.

indicators.note: a cover-up conceals something, so the letters sit concealed in cult ran

explanation.surface: A fanatical sect organised a cover-up.
explanation.definitionFit: An ultra is someone holding extreme views, a synonym for an extremist.

clue.text: Author who's written movingly about the ending

definitions.text: Author who's written movingly about the ending

indicators.note: about means the rearranged letters go round the next piece
written movingly suggests the letters of the word are moved into new places
ending means the last letter of the word the

explanation.surface: A writer whose work describes the end of life with feeling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'written movingly' rearranges AUTHOR, and 'about' puts it round E, the end of 'the'. Thoreau wrote about simple living and civil disobedience.
explanation.definitionFit: Henry David Thoreau, author of Walden, was an American writer and essayist.

indicators.note: dogging means following close behind, so the curses come after the

parts.note: taken as written
ban is an archaic word for a curse

explanation.surface: Ancient curses following the Greeks around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Old' belongs with 'curses': ban is an archaic word for a curse, not part of the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The Thebans were citizens of Thebes, an ancient Greek city-state.

clue.text: Inhabitants of Kazan start a riot

indicators.note: a riot is wild disorder, so these letters are thrown out of order

explanation.surface: The people of a Russian city begin a riot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'riot' rearranges START A. Kazan is the capital of Tatarstan in Russia.
explanation.definitionFit: Kazan is the capital of Tatarstan, home of the Tatar people.

clue.text: Have trouble containing disease and thus let oneself down

indicators.note: containing means the word for have trouble holds the disease

parts.note: to ail is to be unwell or in trouble
BSE is mad cow disease

explanation.surface: A sufferer whose illness makes them disappoint themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: 'let oneself down' sounds like failure; it means a descent on a rope.
explanation.definitionFit: To abseil is to descend a rock face by rope, literally lowering oneself.

indicators.note: cooked means the letters are prepared afresh in a new order

parts.note: a cracking pace is fast

explanation.surface: A baker preparing an excellent meal.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cooked' rearranges BAKER into BREAK.
explanation.definitionFit: Breakfast is the first food of the day, a kind of meal.

definitions.meaning: to tolerate or put up with
Rupert is the cartoon character from the Daily Express, a check-trousered teddy

explanation.definitionFit: To bear something is to put up with it; Rupert is a famous British cartoon of that animal.

clue.text: Musical instrument not unknown in Japanese city

indicators.note: not means the unknown is left out of the city

parts.note: Kyoto is the old imperial capital of Japan
Y is an algebraic unknown

explanation.surface: An instrument that is familiar in a Japanese city.
explanation.definitionFit: The koto is a Japanese long zither with thirteen strings, a musical instrument.

indicators.note: most of means one letter of the word is dropped

parts.note: the masses are the common people

explanation.surface: Most people are idiots.
explanation.definitionFit: Asses are stupid people, a common synonym for fools.

clue.text: It's a horrible old Indian custom

indicators.note: horrible suggests something mangled, so these letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as the letters it is a

explanation.surface: A grim remark about an ancient Indian practice.
explanation.walkthrough: 'horrible' rearranges IT'S A. Sati was a widow's self-immolation on her husband's pyre.
explanation.definitionFit: Sati, the burning of a widow on her husband's pyre, was a former practice in India.

clue.text: A second TV is an advantage

parts.note: a TV set

explanation.surface: Having a spare television is a benefit.
explanation.definitionFit: An asset is a useful quality or resource, a synonym for an advantage.

clue.text: Thief has central part in criminal trials

indicators.note: in means that run sits inside the rearranged letters
criminal suggests the letters are crooked, so they are rearranged
part means a run of letters taken from the word central

explanation.surface: A robber plays the main role in court cases.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' makes LARIST from its fodder; 'part' takes the opening run of 'central', and 'in' sets it inside.
explanation.definitionFit: A larcenist commits larceny, the legal term for theft, so is a thief.
